title: Whether the confirmed controllers' decisions come from the decoder's memory
description: A probe of the controllers grounded in exp-ground-rl-confirm-32 (experiments/ground-rl-confirm.json), on their own rollouts from that release, without new rollouts: for each teacher (Cubic, BBRv3), widths 7, 10 and 16, seeds 1 to 3. In that grounding the change a decision makes was mostly unexplained: the sender's window alone gave 0.11 or less and the best fit on ground truth 0.17 to 0.37, while the decision u itself is read from the latents at 0.87 to 0.98. The candidate that the window in force is not the one the controller set was ruled out there. The candidate left is the decoder's memory: the decoder is recurrent, so a decision depends on the latents and the window at this step and on its hidden state. experiments/ground.py probe fits the change from what the decoder sees at this step, the latents and the window in force, linearly and by a small network (the flexible fit of select, on ranks, inputs standardized), on the training links' rollouts and scored on the validation links' rollouts. The first run of this file (exp-probe-memory-33) used a quadratic fit in place of the network. That fit is left out above 16 inputs, so width 16 had none, and it was unstable elsewhere (an R^2 of -1.13 where the linear fit gave 0.22), so its rule could not be read; the network replaces it, with the same threshold. Rule: if the small network explains more than 0.5 of the change in most runs of a teacher, what the library misses lies in the latents of the step and grounding should look there; if it explains 0.5 or less in most runs, the change comes mostly from the decoder's memory, and grounding the change from one step is the wrong question for that teacher. Everything else the probe reports is as in the release it reads. The test links are not read.
